title: Genetic assimilation of bioelectric phenotypes likely shaped body-plan evolution

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Genetic assimilation of bioelectric phenotypes likely shaped body-plan evolution

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Evolutionary changes in ion channel properties that lead to genetic assimilation of bioelectrically induced phenotypes are likely an important aspect of the evolution of body plans and other morphological features, analogous to the Baldwin effect for learning.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Evolutionary tweaks of ion channel properties that eventually lead to genetic assimilation of bioelectrically induced phenotypes is likely an important aspect of the evolution of body plans and other morphological features, much as the Baldwin effect is thought to be a key dynamic for the role of cognition and learning in evolutionary lineages (Baldwin 1896).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Re-writing morphogenetic memories: ontogenetic and evolutionary timescales”. Scope: Evolution of animal body plans

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.47

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Particular candidate transitions can be investigated with comparative molecular and morphology data. Existing data cannot directly observe the ancestral plastic phase or establish that this was an important general driver of body plans.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across phylogenetically sampled lineages, test whether inherited ion-channel changes stabilize morphologies first inducible by physiological perturbation and whether such transitions exceed matched alternatives. Evidence must establish temporal order from plastic phenotype to heritable channel change.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Historical induction states are not preserved.

The asserted importance across body-plan evolution lacks a quantitative threshold.

Correlated channel and morphology evolution does not establish genetic assimilation.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.48

discriminating power: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Sequences and divergence times are public, but the decisive variables are a plastic bioelectric phenotype and its later genetic assimilation, which are not in those databases. A comparative test is definable and cannot be run on existing open data. The claim stays a historical likelihood rather than a result those resources can confirm or refute.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On a phylogeny, find morphology shifts that match a phenotype first produced by a bioelectric manipulation, and ask whether ion-channel substitutions were fixed afterward and then produce the phenotype without the manipulation. That order would support genetic assimilation; channel changes with no such plastic precursor, or plastic phenotypes that were never genetically fixed, would count against it as an important route to body plans.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No dataset records a bioelectrically induced phenotype and a later genetic fixation of that phenotype.

Likely importance and the Baldwin-effect analogy are not decided by channel sequence divergence.
